summary: Dashboard scope-collection SECONDARY LISTINGS junction (cinatra#1897 B4; the ratified design spec at design@bb9230d9b, specs/app-artifacts.html §IX 'The scope Dashboards tab — listings & add-to-scope') — the operator-upgrade twin of the fresh-install bootstrap DDL in src/lib/drizzle-store.ts (buildCreateStoreSchemaQueries, the dashboard_entity_links CREATE + three indexes, spread in the SAME PR). ONE brand-new table backing the add-to-scope side of the scope Dashboards tab. A dashboard's CANONICAL HOME stays the singular (entity_type, entity_id) on `dashboards` (§VIII); this junction adds a SEPARATE listing relation — a dashboard listed on a team's/project's/organization's Dashboards tab as a reference, never a second home; a listing opens the SAME canonical surface the home does, so the home axis, the Overview default-uniqueness index and the per-entity name-uniqueness index on `dashboards` are all untouched. dashboard_entity_links: one row per (dashboard, scope) listing — dashboard_id FKs dashboards(id) ON DELETE CASCADE (a listing is meaningless without its dashboard); entity_type is the scope kind the dashboard is LISTED in, the three shared add-to-scope scopes ONLY ('team'|'organization'|'project' — a personal user scope and the whole-workspace scope are not add-to-scope targets, §IX; enforced by CHECK); entity_id is the scope instance id; organization_id is the scope's tenant denormalized from the dashboard's org at add time so a per-scope listing query stays tenant-scoped without a join; created_by is the scope manager who added the listing. UNIQUE (dashboard_id, entity_type, entity_id) makes add idempotent (ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING) and remove exact; INDEX (entity_type, entity_id, organization_id) is the tab's per-scope read; INDEX (dashboard_id) is the reverse (scope chips / FK cascade). ADDITIVE (one brand-new empty table + indexes) — the DDL MIRRORS the idempotent bootstrap leaf exactly (CREATE ... IF NOT EXISTS): a no-op on a bootstrap-seeded schema, ledger-faked on a fresh install, executed by db migrate on an existing deployment; unqualified names resolve to the app schema on the runner's search_path. down() drops the fresh table (reversible; carries no data on a fresh install; a canonical home is never a listing, so no dashboard home is ever lost). SEQ 0080 — strictly greater than the max seq VISIBLE across origin/main (core__0075_widget-auth-token-keys-canonical, merged) AND every open PR: PR #1986 currently carries core__0073/0074 (assistants W5) which its own renumber-at-merge bumps to core__0076/0077 (0075 landed on main after #1986 opened), so 0080 clears both the merged tip AND #1986's post-renumber pair; a concurrent lane may land an intervening seq first, in which case a rename-only renumber is normal (FLAGGED for the coordinator's train; the runner tolerates sequence gaps). migrations/** is HIGH-RISK: owner approval required; the lane never merges.
